source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἱερατικούς, ἢ κληρικούς, ἢ λαϊκούς, καλουμένους εἰς ἀγάπην, μέρη αἵρειν, διὰ τὸ τὴν ὕβριν τῇ τάξει προστρίβεσθαι τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ.
thought_title: No taking portions at a love feast
orientation: The council continues its rules on church order, now forbidding clergy and laity invited to a love feast from taking portions.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not right for priests, or clergy, or lay people, when called to a love feast, to take portions, because the insult is brought upon the ecclesiastical order.

choices.why: The brief's cast distinguishes bishops, presbyters, and deacons, but this canon uses a broader term for ordained ministers; 'priests' renders the Greek adjective substantivally without narrowing to presbyters.
The glossary requires 'love feast' for ἀγάπη in this communal meal sense.
The infinitive αἵρειν means to take or carry away; 'portions' preserves the concrete sense of shares of food at the meal.

choices.term: ὕβριν τῇ τάξει προστρίβεσθαι τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ
choices.english: the insult is brought upon the ecclesiastical order
choices.why: The passive infinitive προστρίβεσθαι means to be rubbed against or brought upon; the dative τῇ τάξει τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ is the recipient of the insult, so the passive construction is kept.
rejected: to bring insult upon the ecclesiastical order
the insult attaches to the ecclesiastical order

pass_b_english: Priests, clergy, or lay people who are invited to a love feast must not take portions away with them, because this brings insult upon the order of the church.

last_rejected.quote: because this brings insult upon the order of the church
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ τὸ τὴν ὕβριν τῇ τάξει προστρίβεσθαι τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ
last_rejected.why: ὕβριν means 'outrage/insult' but προστρίβεσθαι is passive: 'to be brought upon', not active 'brings'. Agency reversed.
last_rejected.fix: because insult is brought upon the church's order
last_rejected.ruling: προστρίβεσθαι is middle/passive form but functions causatively here; 'brings insult upon' preserves meaning adequately.
